_note: Public record of times this review was wrong. Rendered on the Method tab once populated. Append-only.

entries.where: claude/source-genealogy.md, Tychonian lineage table, Bouw row
entries.old_argument: Cited creation.com/geocentric-gobbledegook as the source for Bouw's concession that his model is observationally equivalent to heliocentrism.
entries.new_argument: That page is Danny Faulkner reviewing Marshall Hall's 'The Earth is not Moving'. It does not support the Bouw concession. Use the Bouw Wikipedia entry and Faulkner's companion article 'Geocentrism and Creation', Journal of Creation 15(2) 2001, which states the essential difference is a coordinate change from Sun to Earth.
entries.reason: Citation checked against the source and did not say what we attributed to it.

entries.old_argument: Bowden, Journal of Creation 16(2) 2002, pp. 79-82.
entries.new_argument: The PDF paginates 79-81. The quoted concession is on p. 80.
entries.reason: Page range did not match the document.

entries.where: corpus: ARG-C02 originator; and claude/source-genealogy.md by implication
entries.old_argument: Attributed the 16 sun-motion scriptural proof-texts (Joshua 10, Habakkuk 3, Ecclesiastes 1:5, Psalm 19, Isaiah 38) to William Carpenter, One Hundred Proofs (1885).
entries.new_argument: Verified against the full Gutenberg text (143,011 chars): Carpenter's book contains exactly ONE scriptural proof, #50, and it concerns immovability and the stretched-out earth, not the sun's motion. The words Joshua, Habakkuk and Ecclesiastes appear ZERO times in the book. Carpenter's own sun-motion proofs (38, 39) argue from observed appearance. The sun-motion proof-text corpus is a later accretion; C02 reattributed to Rob Skiba's modern biblical-cosmology compilations. C01 (immovability texts) correctly stays with Carpenter.
entries.reason: Attribution asserted from the shape of the genre rather than checked against the primary text.

entries.old_argument: All 15 R06 item titles attributed to Sungenis & Bennett, Galileo Was Wrong Vol. I (2006).
entries.new_argument: Full-text search of the archive.org scan of Vol. I returns ZERO occurrences of 'Noether', 'Fermat', 'light cone'/'lightcone'. 'Gauge' occurs only as Ron Hatch's clock-rate scale factor, not gauge symmetry. 'Renormalization' occurs only as a complaint about QFT infinities, never about frames. 'Anthropic' occurs three times with the authors ATTACKING the anthropic principle, so the item title 'Anthropic coordinate justification' states the REVERSE of the source's stance. At least 6 of 15 item titles are unlocatable in the cited source and are marked as such rather than refuted as the authors' claims.
entries.reason: Cluster-level attribution was applied to every item in the cluster without checking each against the source text.
entries.caveats: The scan is one volume of a multi-volume work; OCR quality is variable; these vocabularies do circulate in downstream forum material. The defensible claim is 'not located in the scanned text of Vol. I', NOT 'the authors never wrote this'.

entries.old_argument: Named the argument "No wind/drag from Earth's motion; atmosphere can't co-rotate" and gave the basis as "Assumes the atmosphere is not gravitationally bound to the Earth. It is."
entries.new_argument: Rowbotham asserts the opposite of what we attributed to him. Earth Not a Globe grants co-rotation outright - "we are compelled to conclude that if the earth revolves, the atmosphere revolves also, and in the same direction" - and argues from inside that concession that no residual effect is felt. Renamed "No wind or drag is felt from the Earth's motion"; basis now answers the real claim via Coriolis deflection. Originator year corrected 1865 to 1881: the atmospheric argument enters with the enlarged 3rd edition.
entries.reason: We refuted the list's one-line fragment instead of the source's sentence, and the fragment states the reverse of the source. This is precisely the failure the hedge rule was introduced to catch, and it was the first thing the rule caught.

entries.old_argument: Both refutations argue against the list's fragments artefact by artefact - GPS, sextants, ephemerides for R08; Noether, Fermat, light cones, gauge symmetry for R06.
entries.new_argument: Neither argument form appears in the cited source. Both refutations have been rewritten. R08 now answers the book's conventionalism first - the Einstein/Infeld sentence with its governing condition restored, and the reply that a conventional choice of origin is not a conventional choice of dynamics - and reaches the 28 artefacts only afterwards, under a heading stating they are the list's addition and not the authors'. R06 now concedes the one sentence the source does supply, states the six unlocatable item titles WITH the caveats (one scanned volume, variable OCR, unresolved volume identity, search not independently re-run) before refuting anything, leaves the anthropic reversal unsettled given Woit's contrary testimony, and addresses the remaining items as claims of unknown authorship. Regression tests pin all of it.
entries.reason: Same failure as A10, caught by the same audit. Recording it before fixing it, because a review about provenance should not be able to correct itself silently. Fixed same week; the A10 headline and TLDR were found to carry the same mis-attribution and were rewritten with them.

entries.where: scripts/clusters.py ARG-A05 - originator year AND published basis line
entries.old_argument: Credited to Zetetic Astronomy: Earth Not a Globe, 1865, with the basis line 'Rowbotham took his pseudonym from the thing he denied.'
entries.new_argument: Both wrong. The parallax argument is NOT in the 1865 edition - 'parallax' occurs there twice, both times in the byline - it is an 1881 third-edition addition, ch. III pp. 82-87. And the pseudonym line is false: Rowbotham was signing himself 'Parallax' by the end of 1849, 32 years before he wrote about stellar parallax, in the generic optical sense (apparent shift with viewpoint) that his own perspective theory depends on. He relied on parallax, he did not name himself after a thing he denied. Line withdrawn and replaced.
entries.reason: A rhetorically attractive line that did not survive checking. Those are the ones most likely to be wrong, which is why it was checked.

entries.where: scripts/clusters.py ARG-B04 - originator year and basis line
entries.old_argument: Credited to Zetetic Astronomy 1849. Basis said Carpenter's proofs 5 and 36 (Cape Hatteras, Chesapeake Bay) reappear as Dubay's 89 and 96.
entries.new_argument: 1849 is impossible: the ancestral passage cites the Port Nicholson light, erected 1859, and the lighthouse table is absent from the 1865 first book edition. It is an 1881 third-edition addition, ch. II pp. 28-35. On the basis line, proof 36 to Dubay 96 holds, but Dubay's 89 is Cape Agulhas and 'Cape Hatteras' does not occur in 200 Proofs at all; Carpenter's proof 5 survives instead in a 2018 Dubay blog post. The lighthouse spine of the cluster is Rowbotham's table, not Carpenter's - the reverse of what the old line implied.
entries.reason: Edition dating never checked against the primary text; a lighthouse erected in 1859 cannot appear in an 1849 pamphlet.

entries.old_argument: Both items credited to Rowbotham, Zetetic Astronomy, 1849.
entries.new_argument: Item 42 is Rowbotham's. Item 384 (river grades) is not: it is absent from the 1849 pamphlet as quoted by Schadewald, 'Nile' does not occur in the 1865 text, and the 1881 General Index has no entry for Nile, Rivers, Amazon or Mississippi. Earliest documented text is Carpenter 1885 proof 4 - 'the Nile, which, in a thousand miles, falls but a foot' - passing near-verbatim into Dubay's proof 5.
entries.reason: We inherited the attribution from the movement's own genealogy rather than checking the primary text. Third instance of this failure mode.

entries.where: scripts/clusters.py ARG-D07 - basis line, originator order and year
entries.old_argument: Basis said: "Blavatsky's claimed source text, the 'Book of Dzyan', is regarded by Buddhist-studies scholars as her own invention." Credited to Blavatsky first, Isis Unveiled, 1877.
entries.new_argument: The Dzyan sentence is withdrawn entirely. It is wrong on three counts: the Stanzas frame The Secret Doctrine (1888), not Isis Unveiled (1877), which is the work this cluster was dated to; the people on record treating it as fabricated are a historian, a 19th-c. critic and a writer on fringe claims, not Buddhist-studies scholars, while the one long-term Sanskrit and Tibetan-Buddhist specialist on the question, David Reigle, reports circumstantial evidence in FAVOUR of authenticity; and no item in the cluster descends from Dzyan in any case. Separately, the twelve items track Hall's 1928 chapter list almost one-for-one, so Hall is the primary originator and the year is 1928.
entries.reason: MAJOR under our own review rules: an unsourced bad-faith attribution, made in the name of a scholarly field that says close to the opposite. It was also irrelevant to every item in the cluster, which is how it survived unchecked.

entries.old_argument: Said the maxim was 'popularised in its modern form by a 1908 Chicago New Thought pamphlet.'
entries.new_argument: Overcredits the Kybalion. The compact English axiom was already free-standing in Blavatsky's Isis Unveiled (1877) - 'As above, so it is below... As in heaven, so on earth.' The Kybalion's contribution was to codify it as one of seven numbered Principles, not to popularise it. Wording corrected.
entries.reason: Precision, not a reversal - but on a page whose product is provenance, 'popularised by' and 'codified by' are different claims about who did what.

entries.where: scripts/clusters.py ARG-E13 - originator recorded as None
entries.old_argument: Recorded with originator=None, originator_work=None, year=None - one of 30 arguments carrying no traceable source, with the basis line 'Named without a stated result or inference.'
entries.new_argument: Three of the six items have a documented ancestor in Sungenis & Bennett. Firmest is item 358 'Cosmic birefringence ecliptic': Galileo Was Wrong Vol. II ch. 10 gives Nodland and Ralston's 1997 polarization-rotation claim three pages under a subheading reading simply 'Birefringence:' and closes by placing the axis 'in the ecliptic plane along the equinox' - the item's two content words, appearing together as that section's heading and its punchline. Item 334 (supernova dimming alternatives) traces to Vol. I ch. 2 citing Riess 1998 and Celerier; item 194 held loosely. Cluster reattributed to Sungenis & Bennett, 2013.
entries.reason: 'Untraced' is a claim we make, and it had been audited on exactly one of thirty clusters. The second test came back the other way. Traced items 366 to 372, Sungenis 128 to 134, the headline pair 42 to 43 percent - all published figures moved because a claim of ours was withdrawn.

entries.where: scripts/clusters.py ARG-E03 - originator_work (recorded 2026-08-08, NOT ACTUALLY APPLIED until 2026-08-09 - see the entry below)
entries.old_argument: Credited to 'The Principle (film)', 2014.
entries.new_argument: The dipole argument is textual, not filmic: thirteen numbered 'Claims and Responses' across Galileo Was Wrong Vol. I ch. 3 and Vol. II ch. 10 (7th ed., 2013). The film contains the least of it. Separately, 'dark flow' and 'bulk flow' occur ZERO times across all three volumes - item 327 traces to DeLano's blog of 18 May 2013, not to the book or the film.
entries.reason: We pointed readers at the artefact with the least of the argument in it.

entries.found_by: curmudgeon full sweep, verified critical finding
entries.where: scripts/clusters.py ARG-E01 and ARG-E03 - and this corrections log itself
entries.old_argument: The batch-7 correction written for ARG-E03 was applied to ARG-E01 instead. E01 silently acquired E03's comment block and E03's originator_work/year ('Galileo Was Wrong (7th ed., 2013)...', 2013), and ten E01 dataset rows were rebuilt and published with them. ARG-E03 was never touched and still read 'The Principle (film)', 2014. The corrections entry logged on 2026-08-08 therefore asserted a location that was false.
entries.new_argument: E01 restored to 'The Principle (film)', 2014. The correction applied to E03, where it belonged, anchored on the cluster key so it cannot slide onto a neighbour again. The earlier entry amended to say it was not applied when logged.
entries.reason: ROOT CAUSE, and it is mechanical rather than a judgement failure: E01 and E03 carried a byte-identical originator/work/year line, and the edit used a Python replace(old, new, 1) whose first match was E01. The test suite did not catch it because the originator string was unchanged, so no derived count moved. TWO LESSONS. (1) Anchor every cluster edit on the cluster key, never on a field line that neighbours may share. (2) This is the failure this project exists to catch - an attribution silently reassigned to the wrong source - committed by us, inside the act of logging a correction, and it stood in published data for a day. It was found by the adversarial sweep, not by the tests, which is the argument for running the sweep.

entries.old_argument: Still published: 'He took the pseudonym "Parallax" - naming himself after the measurement he spent his life denying.'
entries.new_argument: Replaced. He wrote as Parallax from the end of 1849, in the ordinary optical sense his own perspective theory relies on, 32 years before he wrote about stellar parallax. The paragraph now carries the withdrawal explicitly.
entries.reason: The sentence was withdrawn on 2026-08-07 and the withdrawal was rendered on the Method tab of the SAME HTML file that continued to assert it. A retraction is worthless while the retracted sentence is still on the page. A test now pins the phrase count at zero.

entries.old_argument: D07's originator was flipped to 'Manly P. Hall; Helena Blavatsky' in batch 6, and ORIGINATOR_PID was never given that key, so originator_id resolved to None.
entries.new_argument: Key added, mapping to PER-HALL. A test now asserts every originator string in CLUSTERS resolves to a person.
entries.reason: Silent failure with three visible symptoms: the argument card printed 'no named originator' one line above a TLDR naming Blavatsky; the lineage chart lost D07's twelve items; and the prose and the chart disagreed about how many items were untraced. Correcting one field broke a join, and nothing checked the join.

entries.found_by: curmudgeon full sweep, Tier 0 - final item
entries.where: scripts/clusters.py ARG-C02 originator, and scripts/deep_batch2.py C02 refutation section 3
entries.old_argument: C02 credited 'Rob Skiba, 2015', rendering as 'first published by Rob Skiba'. Section 3 of the refutation quoted four headings verbatim ('Earth is a Disk/Circle', 'Earth has 4 Corners/Quarters', 'Earth has Pillars, and hangs on nothing') from a compilation we never named, never linked, and did not list in sources.
entries.new_argument: Attribution WITHDRAWN rather than moved a third time. Bellarmine cites Ecclesiastes 1:5 against Copernicus on 12 April 1615 as evidence the Sun really moves; Galileo's Letter to Christina - which this treatment quotes - replies to that genre; Bouw runs the bloc in 1999; Schadewald catalogued it in 1987. Substituting Bouw was rejected on verification as repeating the error one step upstream. A new cluster state, pre_modern, records that the origin is older than the movement, names the earliest DOCUMENTED use, and lists Schadewald, Bouw and Skiba as repopularisers - distributors, not authors. Section 3 now makes the same point from our own corpus with item numbers a reader can check (414 circle, 420 four corners, 410/415 pillars, 412 hangs on nothing).
entries.reason: Two corrections to one field had already been made and both were wrong, which is the signal that the FIELD was wrong rather than the value. 'First published by' cannot be answered for a proof-text bloc in continuous use since the seventeenth century. Operator's call to add an origin-lost-to-antiquity category, with repopularisation recorded as claims are picked up by successive waves - which is the project's own thesis: few people make these arguments, many carry them. Separately, quoting an uncited compilation on a page about provenance was the exact move we criticise, and it was unnecessary since every verse is already in our numbered corpus.

entries.found_by: curmudgeon sweep, applied in a 15-agent parallel pass
entries.where: 37 confirmed findings across 15 source files (Tiers 1-5 of the sweep)
entries.old_argument: Forty confirmed defects stood in published text after Tier 0 was cleared: a work/quote mismatch on A03, a fabricated quantitative attribution to a named living scholar on A05, an uncited ITU paraphrase on B05, an unlocatable Chrysostom quotation on C07, a Foucault factor-of-two in A10 and A22, TLDRs contradicting their own bodies on A22/A02/E13/D06, and volume mislabels propagating from a single bad work record.
entries.new_argument: 61 edits applied, none skipped. Highlights: A03's passage block now cites the work the quote actually came from (Sungenis & Bennett, not van der Kamp, whose book our own gloss already named); A05's 'as wide as Saturn's orbit' is gone - Saturn appears nowhere in Graney's paper - replaced with the orbit of the Earth; the Foucault pendulum precession is now Omega*sin(phi) and distinguished from the Coriolis parameter 2*Omega*sin(phi); R06 scopes its unlocatable-titles count to 'the volume we were able to search' and states the corrected volume identity in the past tense.
entries.reason: Applied by file, never by argument, with one agent owning each file exclusively - deep_batch2.py alone holds A22, C02 and R08, and concurrent edits to one file is how the E01/E03 misfile was manufactured. Two independent agents in different files derived Rowbotham's refraction error as a factor of SEVEN and both rejected the sweep's own recommendation of five; that agreement, reached separately, is better evidence than either alone. Unscoped absence-claims fell from 11 to 4 and the test ceiling was ratcheted down to match.

entries.old_argument: Both credited originator='Mircea Eliade (misapplied)'. The field is documented as 'the person who introduced this argument into the flat-earth or geocentric canon', so this printed a real historian of religion on the People tab as the author of a flat-earth argument.
entries.new_argument: Withdrawn. Eliade introduced nothing into that canon - he was reporting how myths structure sacred space, and states the governing rule himself: 'the multiplicity, or even the infinity, of centers of the world raises no difficulty for religious thought' (The Sacred and the Profane, ch. 1). originator=None; Eliade moved to real_source, the field for whose genuine work is being cited. Named originators 20 to 19, traced items 356 to 348.
entries.reason: The C02 shape a second time: the FIELD was wrong, so any substituted name would also have been wrong. The parenthetical '(misapplied)' shows we knew, and shipped it anyway - a caveat inside a field whose whole meaning contradicts the caveat. Also reported and NOT fixed: no PER-* id exists for Rene Guenon, who is half of D04's real_source line and carries the strongest form of the argument.

entries.old_argument: The check labelled 'headline 20 authors' asserted the literal string '>20<' and kept passing after the author count became 19.
entries.new_argument: It was matching a table cell containing an ITEM count of 20, not the author count. Replaced with needles that assert a number together with the words giving it meaning, derived from the corpus rather than typed: f'{S["named_originators"]} named', f'{S["total_items"]} items', and so on.
entries.reason: Sixth test in this suite retargeted for pinning a string that meant something else. A test that passes for the wrong reason is worse than no test, because it certifies the thing it is not checking. The rule is now recorded inline: assert the number WITH its words, and derive it.

entries.old_argument: ARG-D01 scored NOT DEMONSTRATED while its own note said the claim was 'false in detail'.
entries.correction: Verdict changed to REFUTED. Three of four items carry an explicit universal quantifier, and a universal falls to one counterexample; six ancient primary witnesses supply them. Eratosthenes dropped from the note - he measured the Earth's shape, not its place.

entries.old_argument: ARG-R02 scored STANDARD PHYSICS ('real, already explained') while its own note said Mach's principle is not a settled part of GR.
entries.correction: Verdict changed to MISLEADING. Bondi and Samuel enumerate eleven inequivalent statements of the principle, some of which GR violates. Counter-case recorded in the record: under Assis's relational mechanics one branch of the cluster is arguably true-but-non-discriminating.

entries.old_argument: ARG-D19 scored UNFALSIFIABLE on the strength of its own CLUSTER NAME ('tuned to human timekeeping'), which reads as a design claim. No source making the design claim could be located.
entries.correction: Verdict changed to MISLEADING. The sourced argument is Rowbotham's eclipse chapter, where the point is that eclipse prediction is theory-independent - checkable, checked, factual core true, inference does not follow. Origin fields HELD rather than filled: crediting Rowbotham would move three published headlines and is an operator decision.

entries.old_argument: ARG-E14 published REFUTED - defined on this page as 'contradicted by a specific measurement' - over solar oblateness and its cycle variation, which is genuinely unresolved in the current literature. We called an open measurement closed, on the topic the cluster is named after.
entries.correction: Verdict changed to MISLEADING, the defensible verdict for the bundle. The per-item reading the treatment argues for cannot be expressed: the schema carries one verdict per cluster. This is the direct opposite of the restraint the page insists on at ARG-E01 for the CMB axis, and it was the most attackable sentence in the cluster.
